report:
## Research Findings

The claim is **well-supported by strong evidence**, not false.

**Pivotal trial (ZOE-70):** In the phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled ZOE-70 trial (NCT01165229), 13,900 adults aged ≥70 were randomized to receive the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) or placebo. Vaccine efficacy against herpes zoster in this age group was 89.8% (95% CI, 84.2–93.7), published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* (Cunningham et al., 2016) — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800. This is one of the largest and most rigorous randomized controlled trials on the topic.

**Long-term durability:** A long-term follow-up study (ZOE-LTFU) tracking more than 7,000 participants from the original ZOE-50/ZOE-70 trials for up to 11 years found vaccine efficacy remained substantial: 73.2% in those vaccinated at age ≥70, and 79.8%–82.0% overall in those ≥50, confirming durable protection well beyond the initial trial period — https://www.thelancet.com/journals/eclinm/article/PIIS2589-5370(25)00173-7/fulltext.

**Regulatory/public health consensus:** Based on this trial evidence, the U.S. CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommends Shingrix as the preferred vaccine for shingles prevention in adults 50 and older, including those over 70 — https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/hcp/vaccine-considerations/index.html.

**Conclusion:** Multiple independent, peer-reviewed, large randomized trials plus long-term follow-up data consistently demonstrate that RZV substantially reduces herpes zoster incidence in adults 70 and older, with efficacy near 90% initially and durable protection (~73%) after a decade. This is a well-established, high-confidence finding in the medical literature — the original claim you doubted is accurate, and there is no credible evidence contradicting it.
